title: Guide — Malta Year 7 and Year 8 Math
question: What do the eight units of Malta Track 3 math cover in Year 7 and Year 8, and what does one worked example from each unit look like?
intro:
Year 7 and Year 8 follow the same eight units, from number to probability; Year 8 returns to each unit and goes one step further. Labels such as 1-1 and 1-2 name the subtopics on these pages, not official syllabus codes. The outline follows Track 3.

**Year 7 — foundations**

- **Unit 1 Number System**
  - 1-1 Place value and ordering
  - 1-2 Factors, multiples, primes, LCM
  - 1-3 Squares and cubes
  - 1-4 Decimals, percentages, negative numbers
- **Unit 2 Numerical Calculations**
  - 2-1 BIDMAS
  - 2-2 Rounding
  - 2-3 Fractions
  - 2-4 Percentages of amounts
  - 2-5 Money and direct proportion
- **Unit 3 Algebra**
  - 3-1 Sequences
  - 3-2 Expressions and brackets
  - 3-3 Substitution
  - 3-4 Simple equations
  - 3-5 Coordinates, straight-line graphs, function machines
- **Unit 4 Measurement**
  - 4-1 Angles
  - 4-2 Metric units
  - 4-3 Areas of rectangles, triangles and compound shapes
  - 4-4 Volume of cubes and cuboids
  - 4-5 Time
- **Unit 5 Euclidean Geometry**
  - 5-1 Angles on parallel lines
  - 5-2 Triangles and quadrilaterals
  - 5-3 Nets
  - 5-4 Constructing triangles
  - 5-5 Shapes on coordinates
- **Unit 6 Transformation Geometry**
  - 6-1 Lines of symmetry
  - 6-2 Quadrilaterals by reflection symmetry
- **Unit 7 Statistics**
  - 7-1 Frequency tables
  - 7-2 Bar charts and Carroll diagrams
  - 7-3 Mean, median, mode, range
- **Unit 8 Probability**
  - 8-1 The language of chance
  - 8-2 Listing outcomes
  - 8-3 Simple probability
  - 8-4 Experimental and theoretical probability

**Year 8 — building on Year 7**

- **Unit 1 Number System**
  - 1-1 Powers
  - 1-2 LCM of three numbers
  - 1-3 Square and cube roots
  - 1-4 Recurring decimals and fractions
- **Unit 2 Numerical Calculations**
  - 2-1 Prime factorisation
  - 2-2 Negative numbers
  - 2-3 Mixed numbers
  - 2-4 Percentage change
  - 2-5 Currency, ratio, proportion, map scales
- **Unit 3 Algebra**
  - 3-1 Signed terms and brackets
  - 3-2 Substitution and changing the subject
  - 3-3 Unknowns on both sides
  - 3-4 Straight lines \(y = mx + c\)
- **Unit 4 Measurement**
  - 4-1 Parallelograms and trapezia
  - 4-2 Circumference and area of a circle
  - 4-3 Compound areas
  - 4-4 Surface area of cubes and cuboids
- **Unit 5 Euclidean Geometry**
  - 5-1 Exterior angles
  - 5-2 Quadrilateral problems
  - 5-3 Nets of prisms and pyramids
  - 5-4 Parts of a circle
  - 5-5 Compass constructions
- **Unit 6 Transformation Geometry**
  - 6-1 Reflections
  - 6-2 Rotational symmetry
  - 6-3 Rotations
  - 6-4 Translations by vectors
- **Unit 7 Statistics**
  - 7-1 Pie charts
  - 7-2 Choosing an average
  - 7-3 Outliers and range
- **Unit 8 Probability**
  - 8-1 Probabilities that add up to 1
  - 8-2 Sample spaces for two events

**Where to start:** Year 7 Units 1–3 (number, calculations, algebra) — every Year 8 unit builds on them.

Official syllabi: [Year 7 Track 3](https://curriculum.gov.mt/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/syllabus_maths_yr07_Track-3_Sept_2026.pdf) · [Year 8 Track 3](https://curriculum.gov.mt/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/syllabus_maths_yr08_Track-3_Sept_2026.pdf) · [all Years 7–8 syllabi](https://curriculum.gov.mt/years-7-and-8-learning-outcomes-programmes-and-syllabi-2/).

questions.title: LCM of two box sizes
questions.prompt: A café sells pastizzi in boxes of 6 and qassatat in boxes of 9. What is the smallest number of each that makes the two totals equal, and how many boxes is that?
steps:
List the multiples of each box size until one number is in both lists:

\[\begin{aligned} 6&:\ 6,\ 12,\ 18,\ 24,\ \dots \\ 9&:\ 9,\ 18,\ 27,\ \dots \end{aligned}\]

The first shared multiple is the LCM. 18 is 3 boxes of 6 and 2 boxes of 9:

\[\text{LCM}(6, 9) = \boxed{18}\]

questions.title: Percentage of an amount
questions.prompt: A school trip to Gozo costs €60. A deposit of 35% is paid first. How much is the deposit?
steps:
Build 35% from easy pieces: 10% of 60 is 6, so

\[30\% = 18, \qquad 5\% = 3\]

Add the pieces, and check with the fraction:

\[35\% = 18 + 3 = \tfrac{35}{100}\times 60 = \boxed{21}\]

The deposit is €21.

questions.title: Term of a sequence
questions.prompt: A hall has 12 chairs in row 1, and each row has 3 more chairs than the row before. How many chairs are in row 10?
steps:
The step is 3, so the rule starts with \(3n\). Row 1 has 12 chairs, so add 9:

\[\text{chairs in row } n = 3n + 9\]

questions.title: Area of an L-shape
questions.prompt: A balcony is a 6 m by 4 m rectangle with a 2 m by 3 m corner cut out. Find the area of the balcony.
steps:
Area of the whole rectangle and of the cut-out corner:

\[6\times4 = 24\ \text{m}^2, \qquad 2\times3 = 6\ \text{m}^2\]

Subtract the corner:

\[24 - 6 = \boxed{18\ \text{m}^2}\]

questions.title: Angles on parallel lines
questions.prompt: A straight road crosses two parallel streets. At the first street one angle is \(65^\circ\). Find the alternate angle and the co-interior angle at the second street.
steps:
Alternate angles (a Z shape) are equal:

\[\text{alternate} = 65^\circ\]

Co-interior angles (a C shape) add up to \(180^\circ\):

\[180^\circ - 65^\circ = \boxed{115^\circ}\]

questions.title: Symmetry of quadrilaterals
questions.prompt: How many lines of symmetry do a rectangle, a rhombus, a kite and a parallelogram have?
steps:
A rectangle folds onto itself along the two lines through midpoints of opposite sides; a rhombus along its two diagonals; a kite along one diagonal only; a parallelogram (not a rectangle or rhombus) never.

\[\text{rectangle, rhombus, kite, parallelogram:}\ \boxed{2,\ 2,\ 1,\ 0}\]

questions.title: Mean, median, mode and range
questions.prompt: A team scores these goals in 8 matches: 1, 4, 2, 0, 2, 6, 2, 3. Find the mean, median, mode and range.
steps:
Order the data and add it up:

\[0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 2,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4,\ 6 \qquad \text{total} = 20\]

Mean = total ÷ count; the median is halfway between the 4th and 5th values; 2 appears most often; range = largest − smallest:

\[\boxed{\text{mean } 2.5,\ \text{median } 2,\ \text{mode } 2,\ \text{range } 6}\]

questions.title: Simple probability
questions.prompt: A bag holds 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green counters. One counter is taken at random. Find P(blue) and P(not green).
steps:
There are \(3 + 5 + 2 = 10\) counters, all equally likely:

\[P(\text{blue}) = \frac{5}{10} = \boxed{\frac12}\]

Not green means red or blue, \(3 + 5 = 8\) counters:

\[P(\text{not green}) = \frac{8}{10} = \boxed{\frac45}\]

questions.title: Terminating or recurring
questions.prompt: Does \(\frac{7}{40}\) give a terminating or a recurring decimal? Find the decimal.
steps:
The fraction is in simplest form, and the denominator has only 2s and 5s, so the decimal terminates:

\[40 = 2^3\times5\]

Divide 7 by 40:

\[\frac{7}{40} = \boxed{0.175}\]

questions.title: Percentage increase
questions.prompt: A season ticket costs €80. Next year the price rises by 15%. What is the new price?
steps:
An increase of 15% keeps 100% and adds 15%, so multiply by 1.15:

\[100\% + 15\% = 115\% = 1.15\]

Apply the multiplier:

\[80\times1.15 = \boxed{92}\]

The new price is €92.

questions.title: Unknowns on both sides
steps:
Expand the bracket:

\[3x + 12 = x + 20\]

Take \(x\) and 12 from both sides, then divide by 2:

\[2x = 8 \quad\Rightarrow\quad \boxed{x = 4}\]

Check: \(3(4 + 4) = 24\) and \(4 + 20 = 24\).

questions.title: Area of a trapezium
questions.prompt: A garden is a trapezium with parallel sides of 8 m and 5 m, 4 m apart. Find its area.
steps:
Area of a trapezium = half the sum of the parallel sides × the distance between them:

\[A = \tfrac12(a + b)h\]

Substitute:

\[A = \tfrac12(8 + 5)\times4 = \boxed{26\ \text{m}^2}\]

questions.title: Exterior angle of a triangle
questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, angle A is \(48^\circ\) and angle B is \(67^\circ\). Side BC is extended beyond C. Find the exterior angle at C.
steps:
An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles opposite it:

\[48^\circ + 67^\circ = \boxed{115^\circ}\]
Check: the interior angle at C is \(180^\circ - 115^\circ = 65^\circ\), and \(48^\circ + 67^\circ + 65^\circ = 180^\circ\).

questions.title: Rotation about the origin
questions.prompt: Rotate the point \((4, 1)\) through \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about the origin.
steps:
A quarter turn anticlockwise sends \((x, y)\) to \((-y, x)\):

\[(4, 1) \to \boxed{(-1, 4)}\]

questions.title: Pie chart angle
questions.prompt: In a survey of 36 students, 15 walk to school. Find the angle of the walking sector in a pie chart.
steps:
The sector takes the same fraction of \(360^\circ\) as the group takes of the class:

\[\frac{15}{36}\times360^\circ = \boxed{150^\circ}\]

questions.title: Two events together
questions.prompt: A fair die is rolled and a fair coin is tossed. Find the probability of an even number and heads.
steps:
The sample space has \(6\times2 = 12\) equally likely outcomes. The favourable ones are 2H, 4H and 6H:

\[P = \frac{3}{12} = \boxed{\frac14}\]
